summary: Quarterly business review and ongoing health check with Lighthouse Media focused on usage trends, a recent cost spike for embeddings, p99 latency variability, and evaluating a Dedicated capacity commit. Action items include cost breakdown, latency benchmarks, and renewal pricing scenarios.
topics: Roadmap items and pilot next steps
questions: What drove the embedding cost increase in May?
Can Dedicated reduce 99th percentile latency below 450ms for our workload?
How does Redwood handle KV cache for multi-tenant prefix cache?
What compliance artifacts are available for audits (SOC 2, ISO)?
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-06-10 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (CSM), Ethan Wong (SE); Aisha Turner (Lighthouse), Miguel Santos (VP Product), Ben Carter (Infra)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining the QBR and health check. we'll do a quick run through usage, costs, reliability, then roadmap and next steps. Priya and Ethan are with me. Aisha, Miguel, Ben, thanks for making time.

[00:18] Aisha (Lighthouse): Thanks, Jordan. Yep, we're keen to understand the May spike and talk about the Dedicated pilot we mentioned.

[00:30] Priya (Redwood): Quick agenda: 1) usage & cost trends, 2) performance & reliability, 3) security/compliance check, 4) pilot / roadmap. We'll surface action items as we go.

[00:45] Miguel (Lighthouse): Sounds good. Our leadership especially wants clarity on cost drivers and whether Dedicated will be worth it.

[01:05] Ethan (Redwood): Great, I'll start with a quick performance snapshot. We pulled the token-level breakdown and latency buckets. For Lighthouse's prod route over May, p50 was ~120ms, p95 ~310ms, p99 was around 780ms on hosted pool due to a handful of long-tail requests and some re-tries. We saw heavier embedding calls that are single-request large vectors which elevated compute.

[01:38] Ben (Lighthouse): 780ms p99 matches what we saw in our logs. The issue seemed to correlate with a batch of synchronous embed calls from the recommender job.

[01:50] Jordan (Redwood): Right, and on the cost front, embeddings are priced per embedding unit and those synchronous high-dim calls can be expensive, plus there was a re-run job that reprocessed history. Priya, can you confirm the cost break?

[02:05] Priya (Redwood): Yes, May's bump is twofold: one-off reprocessing (~32% of the increase) and sustained higher usage for session analytics embeddings (~50%). The remaining delta is a small change in model variant usage where a higher-cost model was selected for a subset of routes. I'll share the spreadsheet after the call.

[02:30] Aisha (Lighthouse): The reprocessing was intentional, but we thought the caching would have cut down cost. Why didn't prefix caching help?

[02:42] Ethan (Redwood): A few things: prefix/KV cache helps for repeated prefixes but these reprocessing jobs were sending distinct historical frames; also we had smaller TTLs configured and a conservative cache key strategy. We recommended increasing TTL and expanding cache key normalization in our December notes — looks like that wasn't applied to the analytics pipeline. Also, the batch size for those embedding calls was very small, so batching didn't amortize the overhead.

[03:08] Miguel (Lighthouse): Ok, so operationally we can tune that. But for production SLAs, we're evaluating Dedicated to get more predictable p99 and lower cost per token. Jordan, what's the expected improvement?

[03:22] Jordan (Redwood): For workloads like yours, Dedicated often improves p99 by 30-60% depending on model and sequence length distribution and gives better unit economics for sustained throughput due to reserved capacity. Ethan can add specifics from your sample run.

[03:35] Ethan (Redwood): From our initial sims, moving the largest inference routes to a Dedicated GPU pool with optimized kernel selection and an aggressive batching policy reduces estimated cost per 1M tokens by roughly 22% and p99 to around ~420-480ms based on your median seq len. That assumes quantization-friendly model variants are acceptable for that route.

[04:00] Ben (Lighthouse): Are there any functionality tradeoffs with quantized model variants? We care about subtle semantic differences in generation.

[04:10] Priya (Redwood): Good callout. Quantization can have a small impact on long-form quality. We usually recommend running a small eval harness on sample prompt sets to check regressions — place emphasis on the prompts that surface edge-case hallucinations. Redwood Optimize can suggest specific quantization profiles that balance cost vs quality.

[04:36] Aisha (Lighthouse): We'll want that eval. Also security — for Dedicated we need to know about VPC, KMS, and audit logs. Are those available?

[04:50] Jordan (Redwood): Yes. Dedicated includes a private VPC option, customer-managed KMS integration, and retention of audit logs with configurable retention windows. We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO docs available — I'll attach them.

[05:05] Miguel (Lighthouse): Any latency impact from VPC egress or private connectivity?

[05:12] Ethan (Redwood): On-prem or VPC setups have the usual network factors. For cloud VPC peering in the same region it's negligible; if you use a cross-region hop or private interconnect with queues there can be added latency. We'll coordinate with Ben on the network topology and run end-to-end tests.

[05:33] Ben (Lighthouse): We'll share our network diagram; may need to involve infra team.

[05:40] Jordan (Redwood): Back to costs — Priya, Miguel, do you have a renewal horizon? Is this a near-term decision?

[05:48] Miguel (Lighthouse): Leadership wants options before end of Q2. So within two weeks.

[05:55] Jordan (Redwood): Understood. We'll prioritize a pricing scenarios doc for Dedicated.

[06:05] Ethan (Redwood): Quick note on reliability: we observed two incidents in April/May where model selection fallback triggered due to capacity contention. Those fell back to a compatible variant but added latency. With Dedicated you avoid multi-tenant contention and fallbacks are less likely. We also can set up canary routing and automatic fallback thresholds.

[06:30] Aisha (Lighthouse): For the fallback behavior, do we get visibility into which requests hit fallback variants?

[06:36] Priya (Redwood): Yes, Console tracing shows per-request model variant, route, and latency bucket. We can add a dashboard tile so your oncall sees fallbacks quickly.

[06:50] Miguel (Lighthouse): On the topic of monitoring, can we get token-level cost by route? That's crucial for product owners.

[06:58] Jordan (Redwood): Yes, we already provide token-level cost per route and per-token breakdowns in Console. Priya will export the May report and include a column mapping to your internal route names.

[07:12] Ben (Lighthouse): Also need our audit logs for compliance review next month. We have SOC 2 questions but may need a deeper artifact.

[07:20] Jordan (Redwood): We'll send SOC 2 and compliance pack; for deeper audits we can coordinate with our security team.

[07:28] Miguel (Lighthouse): Switching to roadmap: our product team is planning an A/B experiment that will double prompts per user for 3 weeks in July; we need to understand cost impact and whether throttling or adaptive batching could mitigate costs.

[07:45] Ethan (Redwood): Adaptive batching and dynamic model selection are good knobs. For short experiments we can route excess traffic to a cheaper variant or enable tighter caching for inferred prefixes. Also consider rate limiting at the client side. We'll prepare a cost estimate for the experiment size.

[08:05] Aisha (Lighthouse): Can Redwood run a mock run with sample traffic? That would help.

[08:10] Ethan (Redwood): Yes, we can run a benchmark using your sample workload. I'll need the dataset and prompt set; Aisha, if you can upload to the shared bucket and grant the test account access, we'll run both hosted and Dedicated sims.

[08:28] Aisha (Lighthouse): Yep, I'll do that after this call.

[08:34] Jordan (Redwood): Great. We should also talk about guardrails and quality monitoring — Redwood Optimize can monitor evals and alert on regressions tied to prompt sets.

[08:45] Miguel (Lighthouse): That's useful. Our main worry is model regressions after a quantization or model swap.

[08:52] Priya (Redwood): We'll set up a regression alert on a set of critical prompts and send diffs on output distribution. That can be part of the pilot acceptance criteria.

[09:04] Ben (Lighthouse): For Dedicated pilot, what's the minimum commit?

[09:09] Jordan (Redwood): For Lighthouse's scale, there's a monthly reserved pool option — typically a 3 to 6 month pilot is common with a smaller commit and then scale up. We'll include a few commit tiers in the pricing doc.

[09:22] Miguel (Lighthouse): If we sign for a pilot, will we get a migration plan? We need runbook, rollback steps, and staging testing.

[09:30] Ethan (Redwood): Yes, our SE team will produce a migration plan, test checklist, and roll-back policy. We also do canary deployment support where a small percentage of traffic runs on Dedicated first.

[09:43] Aisha (Lighthouse): About KMS — can Redwood use our customer-managed keys? We need to ensure no plaintext tokens are stored.

[09:52] Jordan (Redwood): Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported. We can also enable extra audit hooks. We'll coordinate on the KMS config.

[10:00] Miguel (Lighthouse): Are there any network egress costs we should be worried about with Dedicated?

[10:06] Priya (Redwood): If traffic crosses regions or uses interconnect, there could be cloud provider egress costs. We'll map your region choices and include estimated egress in the cost scenarios.

[10:18] Ben (Lighthouse): On the SLA side, do you offer uptime SLAs and latency SLOs for Dedicated?

[10:24] Jordan (Redwood): Yes, Dedicated comes with an SLA for uptime and targeted latency objectives; we'll include SLO language in the proposal.

[10:34] Ethan (Redwood): Quick technical deep-dive note — we noticed your seq length distribution is bimodal: short chat-style sequences and a smaller set of long history prompts. We can route the long-history prompts to a variant optimized for KV cache locality which helps reduce compute and tail latency. There was a mention of KV "cash" earlier in notes — sorry, I mean KV cache.

[10:58] Aisha (Lighthouse): Good. We'll want to see the routing config suggestions.

[11:04] Jordan (Redwood): We'll add a sample routing policy in the playbook.

[11:10] Miguel (Lighthouse): Any blockers for us to start the pilot?

[11:14] Priya (Redwood): Need a small sign-off: 1) MOU for pilot commit level, 2) access to sample dataset, 3) network diagram for VPC. Once we have those we can schedule the pilot kickoff.

[11:26] Aisha (Lighthouse): We'll get the dataset and diagram to you by Friday.

[11:30] Jordan (Redwood): Great. Ethan, can you summarize the benchmark plan?

[11:34] Ethan (Redwood): Plan: run two benchmark passes — one against your current hosted config and one simulated Dedicated with optimized kernel selection, batching, and quantized variants. We'll collect p50/p95/p99, cost per 1M tokens, and note any quality diffs on the eval prompt set. Target completion: 2026-06-17.

[11:56] Ben (Lighthouse): Sounds good. We'll also open a ticket for compliance artifacts.

[12:02] Jordan (Redwood): Quick recap and next steps: Priya will send the cost breakdown for May and Console route mapping; Ethan will run benchmarks and share results; Jordan will draft Dedicated pricing options and SLA language; Aisha will upload sample prompts and provide network diagram. Is that correct?

[12:21] Miguel (Lighthouse): Yes, and we'll review the pricing scenarios with leadership next week.

[12:28] Priya (Redwood): I'll also add a dashboard tile for fallback/model-variant visibility and set the eval alert for critical prompts.

[12:36] Jordan (Redwood): Any final questions or concerns?

[12:40] Aisha (Lighthouse): No more from me — thanks.

[12:43] Miguel (Lighthouse): Thanks, everyone.

[12:45] Jordan (Redwood): Thanks all — we'll follow up with the artifacts. Goodbye.

[12:50] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: some words transcribed imperfectly (e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache), occasional speaker label overlap and filler words preserved.
